---
title: "Reproduce a published HCES estimate"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

# pkgdown renders from vignettes/articles/, so the download chunk writes to vignettes/articles/data/hces
id <- "DDI-IND-MOSPI-NSSO-62Rnd-Sch1.0-2005-06"
zip_file <- file.path(
  "data", "hces", id,
  "Household Consumer Expenditure, July 2005 - June 2006_Csv.zip"
)
```

In this article we use the Household Consumer Expenditure Survey (HCES) of NSS round 62 (July 2005 to June 2006).
We perform these steps:

1. Download the CSV files with mospiR.
2. Read one block with base R.
3. Calculate the average monthly per capita consumer expenditure (MPCE).
4. Compare the result with the value in NSS Report No. 523.

All analysis uses only mospiR and base R.

## Download the CSV archive

`list_files()` shows the files in the dataset.
The portal supplies the data in five formats: CSV, JSON, SAS, SPSS and Stata.

```{r download, eval=FALSE}
library(mospiR)
api_key <- Sys.getenv("MOSPI_KEY")
id <- "DDI-IND-MOSPI-NSSO-62Rnd-Sch1.0-2005-06"

files <- list_files(id, api_key)
csv_zip <- grep("_Csv\\.zip$", files$name, value = TRUE)
csv_zip

zip_file <- download_file(id, csv_zip, file.path("data", "hces", id), api_key,
  .files_cache = files
)
```

```{r download-if-missing, ref.label="download", include=FALSE, eval=!file.exists(zip_file)}
```

## Find the blocks in the archive

The archive has one CSV file for each block of Schedule 1.0.
Blocks 5 to 11 have one row for each item.
Block 3 has one row for each household.

```{r list}
members <- unzip(zip_file, list = TRUE)
basename(members$Name[members$Length > 0])
```

## Read Block 3

The text labels in the files use the Windows-1252 character set.
Thus, set `encoding = "latin1"`.

```{r read}
block3 <- grep("Block 3_", members$Name, value = TRUE)
hh <- read.csv(unz(zip_file, block3, encoding = "latin1"))
dim(hh)
```

The DDI file of the dataset gives the labels of the columns.
These columns are necessary for this article:

| Column | Label |
|--------|-------|
| `Sector` | Rural or Urban |
| `State` | State name |
| `B3_q1` | Household size |
| `B3_q14` | Monthly per capita expenditure (Rs) |
| `WGT_SS_Combined` | Multiplier for the central and state samples together |

```{r peek}
head(hh[, c("HHID", "Sector", "State", "B3_q1", "B3_q14", "WGT_SS_Combined")])
```

## Average MPCE

Average MPCE is the total expenditure of all persons divided by the number of persons.
Thus, give each household a weight of multiplier × household size.

```{r mpce}
avg_mpce <- function(d) weighted.mean(d$B3_q14, d$WGT_SS_Combined * d$B3_q1)
round(sapply(split(hh, hh$Sector), avg_mpce))
```

[NSS Report No. 523](https://mospi.gov.in/sites/default/files/press_release/Press_note_on_NSS_Report_no_523_html.pdf) gives these values for 2005-06:
Rs 625 in rural India and Rs 1171 in urban India.
The values from the unit-level data are the same.

## Average MPCE by State

```{r states}
by_state <- sapply(split(hh, hh$Sector), function(s) {
  sapply(split(s, s$State), avg_mpce)
})
round(by_state[order(by_state[, "Rural"]), ])
```

The report gives the lowest rural value for Chhattisgarh (Rs 429).
It gives the lowest urban value for Bihar (Rs 684).

Some State names in the files are not correct, for example `Andhra Pardesh`, `Gujrat` and `Maharastra`.

## Rounds with CSV files

These HCES rounds have a `_Csv.zip` archive on the portal.
So you can use the same steps for each round.
The block files and the column names can be different in each round.

| Round | idno | Period |
|-------|------|--------|
| NSS 57th | `DDI-IND-MOSPI-NSSO-57Rnd-Sch1.0-2001` | 2001 |
| NSS 58th | `DDI-IND-MOSPI-NSSO-58Rnd-Sch1.0-2002` | 2002 |
| NSS 59th | `DDI-IND-MOSPI-NSSO-59Rnd-Sch1.0-2003` | 2003 |
| NSS 60th | `DDI-IND-MOSPI-NSSO-60Rnd-Sch1-Jan-June2004` | 2004 |
| NSS 61st | `DDI-IND-MOSPI-NSSO-61Rnd-Sch1-July2004-June2005` | 2004-05 |
| NSS 62nd | `DDI-IND-MOSPI-NSSO-62Rnd-Sch1.0-2005-06` | 2005-06 |
| NSS 63rd | `DDI-IND-MOSPI-NSSO-63Rnd-Sch1.0-2006-07` | 2006-07 |
